description: The Red Nacional de Caminos (RNC) is Mexico's official routable road network, produced jointly by the national statistics and geography institute INEGI, the infrastructure and transport ministry SICT and the Mexican Transport Institute IMT, and published by INEGI and on the IMT geospatial platform. Contents: the road network with federal, state and municipal roads, urban streets and paths, toll roads, road junctions (unions) and prohibited manoeuvres for routing; localities linked to the network; toll plazas; kilometre reference posts; bridges, with a separate set of bridges on the toll-free federal network by state grouped by length (6 to 30 m, 30 to 100 m, over 100 m) and CAPUFE bridges; structures such as tunnels; ferry crossings; and points of interest for transport and tourism. Producer: INEGI, SICT and IMT. Coverage: the whole of Mexico, 2025 edition, with earlier editions (2018 to 2023) at INEGI. Format and access: shapefiles for the whole network (about 700 MB zipped) or per layer, downloadable without registration from the IMT platform, which also has a map viewer and dashboard; INEGI offers the same product for GIS use. Licence: published as open government data under INEGI's free-use terms; the IMT page links its own terms and conditions. Caveats: large national files; attribute coding follows the RNC data dictionary, so topology checks are needed before routing. Simulation uses: national road network assignment and accessibility, bridge exposure to earthquakes and hurricanes, and detour analysis when federal roads close. Related records: the North American Rail Network (data-north-american-rail-network) covers the rail side.
